extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants (patent prosecution audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and criteria governing extensions of time, petitions to reset reply periods, and abandonment/express abandonment during U.S. patent prosecution, as described in the MPEP. Covers eligibility, fee rules, timing, evidentiary requirements, and examiner handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time with the payment of a fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136 are possible in reply to most Office actions of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: (A) all extensions in a reexamination proceeding (see 37 CFR 1.550(c) and MPEP § 2265); (B) all extensions during an interference proceeding (but not preparatory to an interference where a claim is suggested for interference); (C) those specific situations where an Office action states that the provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not applicable (e.g., reply to a notice of allowability, in reissue applications associated with litigation, or where an application in allowable condition has nonelected claims and time is set to cancel such claims); and (D) those limited instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take certain actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension fee rules and calculation (37 CFR 1.17(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees for extensions of time are set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) and are cumulative. Fees are subject to a 50% reduction for persons or concerns qualifying as small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant paid an extension fee for a 1-month extension and later needs an additional month, the proper fee is the amount set forth for the 2-month extension less the amount previously paid (fees are cumulative). Include reference to current fee schedule when informing applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive petition / safety net under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3) provides that certain prior submissions will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time to render a concurrent or future reply timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive petition conditions include: (A) a written request previously filed to treat a reply as incorporating a petition for extension; (B) a previously filed authorization to charge required fees or extension fees; or (C) submission of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) with the reply. This is a change in practice to avoid loss of rights when petition was inadvertently omitted. The Office nevertheless strongly recommends including a written petition in the reply to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible content/format of a petition for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper petition for extension may be a short written request requesting the Commissioner to extend time for reply, and must indicate the Office action date, number of months, and fee/deposit-account information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example petition language provided: 'The applicant herewith petitions the Commissioner of Patents and Trademarks to extend the time for reply to the Office action dated ____ for ____ month(s) from ____ to ____. Submitted herewith is a check for $____ ... [Please charge my deposit account number ____ in the amount of $ ____].' Examiners are advised to enclose a copy of the fee schedule when using form paragraphs for pro se applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rule: petition/fee filing date determines extension period (37 CFR 1.136(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the petition and the fee have been filed is the date for purposes of determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a) need not be accompanied by a reply (e.g., when extension is for copendency with a continuing application). However, a reply must be filed prior to the expiration of the extended period to avoid abandonment (35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office practice to construe petitions requesting insufficient extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition requests an insufficient period such that filing would be outside the so-extended period, but the period could be further extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a), the Office will construe the petition as requesting the period necessary to make the petition filed within the further extended period if an authorization to charge fees or a deposit-account authorization is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a late-filed two-month petition may be treated as requesting three months when fee authorization exists so the petition is considered timely under the further extended period. This practice applies even if no further reply (appeal brief or CPA) is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must be filed in the application to which it pertains
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for an extension of time must be directed toward and filed in the application to which it pertains in accordance with 37 CFR 1.4 and 1.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition, extension fee, or fee authorization in a continuing application will not effect an extension in the prior application; applicants are cautioned accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late reply acceptance contingent on petition and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reply is filed after the set period for reply and no petition or fee accompanies it, the reply will not be accepted as timely until the petition (which may be constructive under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3)) and the appropriate fee are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: action sets 3-month period; applicant replies in 4th month but includes only petition for 1-month extension — reply not acceptable until fee is filed; if fee filed in 5th month additional fee for the 2nd month extension required to render reply timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extension needed for supplemental reply after complete initial reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136 is not necessary when submitting a supplemental reply to an Office action if a complete first reply was timely filed in reply to the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for cause under 37 CFR 1.136(b): timing, decision, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When 37 CFR 1.136(a) does not apply, extensions for cause under 37 CFR 1.136(b) may be possible but must be filed on or before the day the reply is due and are decided by the Technology Center (TC) Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of such a request will not effect an extension; no extension can operate beyond the 6-month statutory period. Extensions under 1.136(a) or (b) are not available to extend time to submit an oath or declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63, to submit formal drawings, or to make a deposit of biological material, nor to extend the time period set in a Notice of Allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling duplicate requests under 37 CFR 1.136(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for extension under 37 CFR 1.136(b) is filed in duplicate and accompanied by a stamped return-addressed envelope, the Office will indicate the action taken on the duplicate and return it promptly in the envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notation on the original (file record) should be signed by the person granting or denying the extension; the copy returned should also note the action and include the name and title of the person making the notation. Utilization of this procedure is optional on the part of applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of grant/denial and computation of new due date
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request for extension is granted, the due date is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action (remailing date), not from the original due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an action dated Nov 30 gives a 3-month shortened statutory period expiring Feb 28; if extended an additional month, the due date becomes March 30 (not March 28). When request is granted in part, extent of extension is indicated on originals and returned copy; when denied, reason is indicated or formal decision letter provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal delivery and date stamping procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of time may be personally delivered and left with the appropriate area to become an official paper in the file without routing through the Mail Center; the person accepting the request will date stamp it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If duplicate copies hand-delivered to a TC, both copies are dated, stamped approved/approved in part/denied and signed; duplicate copy returned to deliverer regardless of signer status (registered attorney/agent, applicant, assignee). If not presented in duplicate, applicant should be advised promptly of action taken so file record is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs when reply late but extension possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.98 and 7.98.01 may be used where a reply is filed late but an extension of time is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.98 advises applicant that reply was received after expiration and application will become abandoned unless applicant obtains an extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a). 7.98.01 is tailored for pro se applicants and details fee schedule and statutory maximums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection — special timing and examiner language
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant initially replies within 2 months from a final rejection with a 3-month shortened period and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month period, the period for reply for fee calculation purposes will be the date the advisory action is mailed, but cannot extend beyond 6 months from the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must include specified language in each final rejection explaining the shortened statutory period, the special rule for initial replies filed within two months, calculation from advisory action mailing date, and the 6-month maximum statutory limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to submit affidavits after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When an extension is requested after final rejection to submit an affidavit, granting the extension is without prejudice to the examiner questioning why the affidavit is now necessary and why it was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant's showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit despite granting the extension. Grant of extension serves to keep application from becoming abandoned and allows applicant to present the affidavit, but admission/refusal of affidavit will not operate to save the application from abandonment. Affidavits after final rejection are treated like amendments after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions of time after payment of issue fee / post-allowance informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory (nonextendable) time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151); extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are NOT available to correct informalities outstanding at allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informalities (drawing corrections, supplemental declarations, etc.) must be corrected and issue fee paid within the 3-month period; extensions are not available to correct such informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when two periods for reply run concurrently
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply run against an application (regular statutory period and a limited period set in a subsequent Office action), the running of the first period is not suspended or affected by the ex parte limited time action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception referenced at MPEP § 2305.03. Example: when claims copied from a patent are rejected and other claims have an unanswered rejection, the controlling statutory date is the date of the last unanswered Office action on the claims other than the copied patent claims. See Ex parte Milton and MPEP § 2305.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing when reply due date falls on Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: When the last day for taking any action or paying any fee in the USPTO falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken or fee paid on the next succeeding business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.7. Applicable also to provisional application 12-month pendency if the 12-month anniversary falls on weekend/holiday. Federal holidays list (5 U.S.C. 6103) provided. File endorsement should indicate receipt date and note the holiday/weekend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reset/restart of reply period for defective Office actions (incorrect citation, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an Office action contains a defect (e.g., incorrect citation) and the error is called to the Office's attention within 1 month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected if requested by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If error is brought to attention after 1 month but within the reply period, the Office will set a new period substantially equal to the time remaining (new period must be at least 1 month and runs from the date the error is corrected). If called to attention after the reply period has expired, the period will not be restarted and any appropriate extension fee will be required to render a reply timely. See MPEP § 707.05(g) for correcting the record of erroneous citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of remailing or supplementary actions on reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: When an action is remailed, the action should be redated and the remailing date establishes the beginning of the period for reply. A supplementary action after a rejection that explains references more fully establishes a new date from which the statutory period runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Gourtoff and related authority. If correspondence from the Office is received late due to mail delays or USPTO delays, applicants may petition to reset period according to specific guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to reset period due to late receipt of Office action — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the previously set period to run from date of receipt at the correspondence address when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of receipt; (B) a substantial portion of the reply period had elapsed on date of receipt (e.g., at least 1 month of a 2- or 3-month reply period); and (C) petition includes evidence of date of receipt and a statement explaining the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence can be copy of Office action stamped with date of receipt at correspondence address, copy of envelope stamped, etc. Authority to decide such petitions delegated to TC Director where action involved a Technology Center. See Notice 'Petition to reset a period for response due to late receipt of a PTO action'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to reset period due to postmark later than mail date — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the period to run from the postmark date shown on the Office mailing envelope when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of receipt at correspondence address; (B) the reply period was for payment of the issue fee, or the reply period set was 1 month or 30 days; and (C) petition includes evidence of receipt date, copy of envelope showing postmark date, and a statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10 apply regarding filing within 2 weeks. The Office may find such showings insufficient where circumstances point to internal delay rather than mail delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply and related salvage rules (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise. Prosecution to save the application must include such complete and proper reply as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission or refusal to admit amendments after final rejection or amendments not responsive to the last action will not operate to save the application from abandonment. However, where the reply is a bona fide attempt substantially a complete reply but inadvertently omits consideration/compliance with some matter, applicant may be given a new time period to supply the omission (37 CFR 1.135(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment requirements and examiner acknowledgement (37 CFR 1.138)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration of abandonment identifying the application; abandonment must be signed by an authorized party and is effective when an appropriate Office official takes action thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered attorney/agent not of record acting in representative capacity when filing a continuing application may expressly abandon the prior application as of the continuing filing date. To avoid unintended consequences, attorneys/agents must take care to ensure abandonment aligns with applicant's desires and that the appropriate application is identified. Examiners should acknowledge proper express abandonments (form paragraph 7.88) and explain deficiencies if the letter does not comply (form paragraph 7.89). Special note: express abandonments are treated as deliberate acts by the Office.
